summary: The incident triage board: three columns (Open, Investigating, Resolved) holding the incidents created by the correlation engine. It loads `GET /incidents?limit=300`, and dragging a card to another column sends `PATCH /incidents/{id}`; the move appears immediately and is rolled back if the request fails. The board stays live through `live:incident` and the drawer's `incident:changed` event, uses keyed FLIP so re-rendered cards glide to their new places, and gives the animated border beam to the single most urgent card only.

notes.text: Header comment: incidents can be triaged by dragging a card or from the drawer, and only one card, the most urgent, gets the animated border beam, so the board directs attention instead of competing for it.
API helpers `get` and `patch`, plus the app-wide `bus`, used to listen for `incident:changed` directly.
DOM helpers and motion: `enter` for card entrances, `animate` for the live highlight, and `flipKeyed`, which animates a re-rendered list by matching old and new elements on a data attribute.
The segmented control (`seg` builds it, `bindSeg` wires it up), the severity badge `sev` and `icon`.
`toast` for move confirmations and errors; `openIncident` opens the incident drawer.
Column definitions as `[status, label, hint]`. The status keys are the exact values the API stores and accepts: `OPEN`, `INVESTIGATING` and `RESOLVED`.
Only the 12 most recently updated resolved incidents are shown by default, so closed-out history doesn't make the board very long.
A numeric rank per severity, used to sort CRITICAL cards above HIGH, and so on.

`card` renders one incident as an `article` element. `draggable` enables native drag-and-drop, `data-id` is the key for FLIP and dragging, `data-severity` lets the beam find a critical card, and `tabindex=0` makes cards keyboard-focusable; the `lvl-…` class draws the coloured left edge.
Top row: severity badge, incident ID and a grip icon hinting that the card can be dragged. Then the incident title.
Meta line: customer, peak score, number of correlated events and, pushed to the right, how long ago the incident was updated. The last line closes the card.
Page module titled `Incidents`; `render` receives the view element and the cleanup context.

Loads up to 300 incidents, most recently updated first. This array is the board's single source of truth: every redraw is computed from it. It is a `let` because a brand-new incident replaces it with a longer array.
UI state: the active severity filter (empty means all) and whether the user has expanded the Resolved column.
Page header with the title and an explanation of correlation: risky events for the same customer within 30 minutes are merged into one incident, which is the backend's `CORRELATION_WINDOW`.
A severity filter (All, Critical, High, Medium) in the header actions. The last line closes the header.
The board: one `section` per column, each with a header (status pill, hint and an empty count badge) and an empty `data-body` that `draw` fills. The last line closes the board and the template.

`draw` re-renders every column from the `incidents` array. Cards are never patched in place: the markup is recomputed from the data, so what you see always matches the state. `animateCards` asks for the entrance animation.
For each column, finds its element and keeps the incidents that have that status and match the severity filter.

Active columns sort most severe first, then by higher score, then by most recent update; ISO timestamps sort correctly as strings, which is why `localeCompare` works. Resolved keeps the API's order, newest first.
Remembers the full count, truncates Resolved to 12 unless it was expanded, and writes the full count into the column badge.
Mounts the cards. A truncated Resolved column ends with a `Show N more` button, and an empty column shows a calm `Nothing here` placeholder. The last line closes the loop.

The border beam: picks the first CRITICAL card in the Open column (after sorting, the most urgent incident) and appends a decorative `.beam-ring` that CSS animates as a red light travelling around the edge. Because `draw` rebuilds every card, the beam always lands on whichever card is most urgent right now.
Plays the staggered card entrance only when asked (first load and filter changes). Moves animate with FLIP instead, so cards don't fade in again whenever one moves.
The first draw plays the entrance animation. The severity filter then updates `filter` and redraws, again with the entrance.
`move(id, toStatus)` changes one incident's status. It does nothing if the incident is unknown or the card was dropped back on its own column.

Remembers the old status for rollback, then updates local state **optimistically** inside `flipKeyed`. Plain `flip` tracks DOM nodes, which `draw()` throws away, so `flipKeyed` matches cards by `data-id` instead and each card glides from its old spot to its new one.
Saves the change with `PATCH /incidents/{id}` and confirms with a toast coloured by severity, for example `INC-0042 → investigating`.
If the request fails (offline, or a 401 because no API key is set), restores the previous status and redraws, so the card snaps back to where it came from.
Shows an error toast with the API's message, then closes the `catch` block and `move`.
Native HTML5 drag-and-drop. `dragged` holds the ID of the card being dragged, or `null`.
`dragstart` is delegated on the view and ignores anything that isn't an incident card.
Remembers which incident is moving and adds the `dragging` class, which CSS uses to fade the original card to 40%.
Declares a move operation (so the cursor shows move, not copy) and puts the ID on the drag data. Firefox won't start a drag without a `setData` call; the drop handler itself reads `dragged`.

`dragend` fires whether or not the drop succeeded. It removes the fade, forgets the dragged card and clears any column highlight. Forgetting matters: after a cancelled drag, dropping a file or some text on a column used to move the stale card.
`dragover` fires continuously during a drag. It ignores positions outside a column and drags that didn't start on a card, such as files or selected text.
Calling `preventDefault()` here is what tells the browser this column accepts a drop. The hovered column gets the `drop` class (an accent border) and every other column loses it.
`drop` on a column: `preventDefault()` stops the browser's default handling of dropped data (such as opening dropped text as a link), then the highlight is removed.
Calls `move` with the column's status key and clears `dragged`.
Delegated clicks: `Show N more` expands the Resolved column and redraws without animation.
A click anywhere else on a card opens its incident drawer.
Keyboard support: pressing Enter on a focused card opens its drawer too. `closest?.` guards against event targets that have no `closest` method.

Live updates. `live:incident` arrives whenever the correlation engine opens or updates an incident, and after any status change, because the PATCH endpoint re-broadcasts the incident (your own drags included).
Checks whether the board already holds this incident.
Inside `flipKeyed`: merges the new fields into the existing incident, or puts a brand-new incident at the front of the array.
Redraws the board. `flipKeyed` then glides existing cards to their new positions and fades and scales new ones in.
Highlights the updated card with a teal ring that fades out over 1.6 s, then removes the inline style, so the user can see which card just changed. The last line closes the subscription.

`incident:changed` is emitted by the incident drawer when its status control is used. `bus.on` returns an unsubscribe function and `ctx.add` registers it, which is exactly what `ctx.on` does in one call.
If the local copy has a different status, applies the new one with the same FLIP animation, so a change made in the drawer moves the card behind it.
Closes `render` and the page object.
